chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from al-Qasim al-Nahdi, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from al-Kunasi, from Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام), who said:

Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali (عليه السلام) went out during part of his lifetime, and with him was a man from the descendants of al-Zubayr who believed in his Imamate. They halted at a watering place among those watering places, beneath a dry palm tree that had withered from thirst.

A place was spread for al-Hasan (عليه السلام) beneath one palm tree, and a place was spread for al-Zubayri opposite him beneath another palm tree. He said: al-Zubayri then said, raising his head, 'If there were fresh dates on this palm tree, we would eat from it.' So al-Hasan said to him, 'Do you truly desire fresh dates?' Al-Zubayri said, 'Yes.'

He said: so he raised his hand toward the sky and supplicated with words that I did not understand. The palm tree became green, then returned to its proper state, putting forth leaves and bearing fresh dates. The camel-driver from whom they had hired said, 'By Allah, this is sorcery.' Al-Hasan (عليه السلام) said, 'Woe to you, it is not sorcery; rather, it is the answered supplication of the son of a Prophet.'
He said: then they climbed the palm tree and harvested what was on it, and it was sufficient for them.

key_terms.إِمَامَتِهِ: his divinely appointed leadership and authority
key_terms.دَعْوَةُ: a supplication or prayer made to Allah
key_terms.رُطَبٌ: fresh ripe dates on the palm tree
key_terms.سِحْرٌ: sorcery, falsely alleged by the camel-driver
key_terms.فَاخْضَرَّتِ: it became green after being dry
key_terms.مَنْهَلٍ: a watering place or stopping point for travelers

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show the accepted supplication and miraculous sign of Imam al-Hasan (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This narration recounts a sign manifested at the hands of al-Hasan ibn 'Ali (عليه السلام), when a dry palm tree became green and bore fresh dates after his supplication. It highlights his Imamate, the acceptance of the supplication of the Ahl al-Bayt (عليهم السلام), and distinguishes divine grace from sorcery.
